content.content:
version: 2

models:
  - name: stg_regions
    description: Cleaned region records. One row per region (5 regions).
    columns:
      - name: region_id
        description: Unique region identifier.
      - name: region_name
        description: Region name (AFRICA, AMERICA, ASIA, EUROPE, MIDDLE EAST).
      - name: region_comment
        description: Free-text comment about the region.

  - name: stg_nations
    description: Cleaned nation records. One row per nation (25 nations).
    columns:
      - name: nation_id
        description: Unique nation identifier.
      - name: nation_name
        description: Nation name (e.g. UNITED STATES, GERMANY, CHINA).
      - name: region_id
        description: Foreign key to stg_regions.
      - name: nation_comment
        description: Free-text comment about the nation.

  - name: stg_customers
    description: Cleaned customer records. One row per customer.
    columns:
      - name: customer_id
        description: Unique customer identifier.
      - name: customer_name
        description: Customer name (format Customer#NNNNNNNNN).
      - name: customer_address
        description: Street address of the customer.
      - name: nation_id
        description: Foreign key to stg_nations.
      - name: customer_phone
        description: Phone number (format NN-NNN-NNN-NNNN).
      - name: account_balance
        description: Account balance in dollars. May be negative.
      - name: market_segment
        description: Market segment (AUTOMOBILE, BUILDING, FURNITURE, HOUSEHOLD, MACHINERY).
      - name: customer_comment
        description: Free-text comment about the customer.

  - name: stg_orders
    description: Cleaned order records. One row per order.
    columns:
      - name: order_id
        description: Unique order identifier.
      - name: customer_id
        description: Foreign key to stg_customers.
      - name: order_status
        description: "Order status: F = fulfilled, O = open, P = partially fulfilled."
      - name: total_price
        description: Total order price in dollars.
      - name: order_date
        description: Date the order was placed.
      - name: order_priority
        description: "Priority: 1-URGENT, 2-HIGH, 3-MEDIUM, 4-NOT SPECIFIED, 5-LOW."
      - name: clerk
        description: Clerk who processed the order.
      - name: ship_priority
        description: Shipping priority flag (integer).
      - name: order_comment
        description: Free-text comment about the order.

  - name: stg_line_items
    description: "Cleaned line item records. One row per line item (order + line number). The most granular fact table."
    columns:
      - name: order_id
        description: Foreign key to stg_orders.
      - name: line_number
        description: Line number within the order (1-based).
      - name: part_id
        description: Foreign key to stg_parts.
      - name: supplier_id
        description: Foreign key to stg_suppliers.
      - name: quantity
        description: Quantity ordered (1 to 50).
      - name: extended_price
        description: Line item price before discount (quantity * retail price).
      - name: discount
        description: Discount percentage as a decimal (0.00 to 0.10).
      - name: tax
        description: Tax rate as a decimal (0.00 to 0.08).
      - name: return_flag
        description: "Return status: R = returned, A = accepted, N = not yet received."
      - name: line_status
        description: "Shipping status: F = shipped, O = not yet shipped."
      - name: ship_date
        description: Date the line item was shipped.
      - name: commit_date
        description: Committed delivery date.
      - name: receipt_date
        description: Actual date the customer received the item.
      - name: ship_instructions
        description: Shipping instruction (DELIVER IN PERSON, COLLECT COD, TAKE BACK RETURN, NONE).
      - name: ship_mode
        description: Shipping mode (AIR, FOB, MAIL, RAIL, REG AIR, SHIP, TRUCK).
      - name: line_item_comment
        description: Free-text comment about the line item.

  - name: stg_suppliers
    description: Cleaned supplier records. One row per supplier.
    columns:
      - name: supplier_id
        description: Unique supplier identifier.
      - name: supplier_name
        description: Supplier name (format Supplier#NNNNNNNNN).
      - name: supplier_address
        description: Street address of the supplier.
      - name: nation_id
        description: Foreign key to stg_nations.
      - name: supplier_phone
        description: Phone number (format NN-NNN-NNN-NNNN).
      - name: account_balance
        description: Account balance in dollars.
      - name: supplier_comment
        description: Free-text comment about the supplier.

  - name: stg_parts
    description: Cleaned part records. One row per part.
    columns:
      - name: part_id
        description: Unique part identifier.
      - name: part_name
        description: Part name composed of randomly generated words.
      - name: manufacturer
        description: Manufacturer name (format Manufacturer#N).
      - name: brand
        description: Brand name (format Brand#NN).
      - name: part_type
        description: Part type as a 3-word compound (e.g. STANDARD POLISHED BRASS).
      - name: part_size
        description: Part size as an integer from 1 to 50.
      - name: container
        description: Shipping container type (e.g. SM CASE, LG BOX, MED PKG).
      - name: retail_price
        description: Retail price per unit in dollars.
      - name: part_comment
        description: Free-text comment about the part.

  - name: stg_part_suppliers
    description: Cleaned part-supplier records. One row per part-supplier combination.
    columns:
      - name: part_id
        description: Foreign key to stg_parts.
      - name: supplier_id
        description: Foreign key to stg_suppliers.
      - name: available_quantity
        description: Units available from this supplier for this part.
      - name: supply_cost
        description: Cost per unit from this supplier, in dollars.
      - name: partsupplier_comment
        description: Free-text comment about this part-supplier relationship.
version: 2

models:
  - name: order_summary
    description: "Enriched order-level summary joining orders with customer, nation, region, and aggregated line item metrics. One row per order."
    columns:
      - name: order_id
        description: Unique order identifier.
      - name: order_date
        description: Date the order was placed.
      - name: order_status
        description: "Order status: F = fulfilled, O = open, P = partially fulfilled."
      - name: order_priority
        description: "Priority: 1-URGENT, 2-HIGH, 3-MEDIUM, 4-NOT SPECIFIED, 5-LOW."
      - name: customer_name
        description: Name of the customer who placed the order.
      - name: market_segment
        description: Market segment of the customer.
      - name: customer_nation
        description: Nation where the customer is located.
      - name: customer_region
        description: Geographic region where the customer is located.
      - name: total_price
        description: Total order price in dollars as recorded on the order.
      - name: line_item_count
        description: Number of line items in the order.
      - name: total_quantity
        description: Sum of quantities across all line items.
      - name: gross_revenue
        description: Sum of extended prices before discounts.
      - name: net_revenue
        description: Revenue after discount. sum(extended_price * (1 - discount)).
      - name: total_with_tax
        description: Net revenue plus tax. sum(extended_price * (1 - discount) * (1 + tax)).

  - name: supplier_performance
    description: "Supplier-level performance metrics including revenue, quantity supplied, and supply cost aggregates. One row per supplier."
    columns:
      - name: supplier_id
        description: Unique supplier identifier.
      - name: supplier_name
        description: Name of the supplier.
      - name: supplier_nation
        description: Nation where the supplier is located.
      - name: supplier_region
        description: Geographic region where the supplier is located.
      - name: orders_fulfilled
        description: Count of distinct orders this supplier contributed to.
      - name: total_quantity_supplied
        description: Total quantity of items supplied across all orders.
      - name: total_revenue
        description: Gross revenue (sum of extended prices).
      - name: net_revenue
        description: Revenue after discounts.
      - name: avg_item_price
        description: Average extended price per line item.
      - name: min_supply_cost
        description: Lowest supply cost across all parts this supplier provides.
      - name: avg_supply_cost
        description: Average supply cost across all part-supplier relationships.
      - name: total_available_quantity
        description: Total inventory available across all parts.

  - name: revenue_by_region
    description: "Revenue and order metrics aggregated by region and nation. Useful for geographic analysis of sales performance."
    columns:
      - name: region_name
        description: Geographic region name.
      - name: nation_name
        description: Nation name within the region.
      - name: customer_count
        description: Number of distinct customers with orders.
      - name: order_count
        description: Number of distinct orders.
      - name: net_revenue
        description: Total revenue after discounts.
      - name: avg_order_value
        description: Average total_price per order.

  - name: customer_lifetime_value
    description: "Customer-level lifetime value metrics including total spend, order frequency, and product diversity. One row per customer. Includes customers with zero orders."
    columns:
      - name: customer_id
        description: Unique customer identifier.
      - name: customer_name
        description: Name of the customer.
      - name: market_segment
        description: Market segment the customer belongs to.
      - name: customer_nation
        description: Nation where the customer is located.
      - name: customer_region
        description: Geographic region where the customer is located.
      - name: account_balance
        description: Current account balance in dollars. May be negative.
      - name: total_orders
        description: Total number of orders placed by this customer.
      - name: first_order_date
        description: Date of the customer's earliest order.
      - name: last_order_date
        description: Date of the customer's most recent order.
      - name: lifetime_net_revenue
        description: Total revenue after discounts across all orders.
      - name: lifetime_quantity
        description: Total quantity of items ordered.
      - name: avg_order_value
        description: Average total_price per order.
      - name: revenue_per_order
        description: Lifetime net revenue divided by total orders.
      - name: total_line_items
        description: Total number of line items across all orders.
      - name: distinct_parts_ordered
        description: Number of unique parts this customer has ordered.
      - name: distinct_suppliers_used
        description: Number of unique suppliers that fulfilled this customer's orders.

  - name: shipping_analysis
    description: "Shipping and delivery performance metrics aggregated by ship mode, region, and nation. Tracks delivery timeliness, late delivery rates, and return rates."
    columns:
      - name: ship_mode
        description: Shipping mode (AIR, FOB, MAIL, RAIL, REG AIR, SHIP, TRUCK).
      - name: customer_region
        description: Geographic region of the receiving customer.
      - name: customer_nation
        description: Nation of the receiving customer.
      - name: shipment_count
        description: Total number of line items shipped in this group.
      - name: total_quantity_shipped
        description: Total quantity of items shipped.
      - name: net_revenue
        description: Revenue after discounts for this group.
      - name: avg_delivery_days
        description: Average days between ship date and receipt date (transit time).
      - name: avg_receipt_vs_commit_days
        description: "Average days between committed date and receipt date. Negative = early, positive = late."
      - name: avg_days_to_ship
        description: Average days between order date and ship date (fulfillment speed).
      - name: late_deliveries
        description: Number of line items received after the committed date.
      - name: late_delivery_rate
        description: Fraction of line items delivered late (0.0 to 1.0).
      - name: returned_items
        description: Number of line items with return_flag = R.
      - name: return_rate
        description: Fraction of line items returned (0.0 to 1.0).

  - name: part_pricing_analysis
    description: "Product pricing and supply chain metrics aggregated by part type, brand, manufacturer, and container. Combines catalog pricing with sales data and supply costs."
    columns:
      - name: part_type
        description: Part type category (e.g. STANDARD POLISHED BRASS).
      - name: brand
        description: Brand name (format Brand#NN).
      - name: manufacturer
        description: Manufacturer name (format Manufacturer#N).
      - name: container
        description: Shipping container type (e.g. SM CASE, LG BOX).
      - name: part_count
        description: Number of distinct parts in this category.
      - name: avg_retail_price
        description: Average retail price across parts.
      - name: min_retail_price
        description: Lowest retail price.
      - name: max_retail_price
        description: Highest retail price.
      - name: supplier_count
        description: Number of distinct suppliers for this category.
      - name: avg_supply_cost
        description: Average cost per unit from suppliers.
      - name: avg_margin
        description: Average retail price minus supply cost (gross margin per unit).
      - name: total_available_inventory
        description: Total units available across all suppliers.
      - name: total_quantity_sold
        description: Total units sold. Zero if no sales.
      - name: total_net_revenue
        description: Total revenue after discounts. Zero if no sales.
      - name: avg_discount_applied
        description: Average discount rate on line items in this category.
----

105	def finalize_dbt_artifacts(
106	    dbt_project_path: str,
107	    dbt_target_path: str,
108	    s3_bucket: str,
109	    s3_prefix: str,
110	    run_id_raw: str,
111	):
112	    """Merge per-task run_results shards, regenerate manifest+catalog via
113	    dbt docs generate, publish all three canonical artifacts to S3, and delete
114	    the shard prefix.
115	
116	    Runs inside a PythonVirtualenvOperator with dbt-trino + boto3 installed
117	    into the venv. Fully self-contained — imports live inside the body because
118	    the callable is serialized into a subprocess, and we avoid `airflow.*`
119	    imports entirely because uv's venv doesn't inherit the Stackable Airflow
120	    image's site-packages reliably. The garagefs connection is read straight
121	    from the AIRFLOW_CONN_GARAGEFS env var (which Airflow sets on executor
122	    pods from the garagefs-airflow-credentials secret).
123	    """
124	    import json
125	    import os
126	    from pathlib import Path
127	    from urllib.parse import quote, urlparse, parse_qs, unquote
128	    import boto3
129	    from dbt.cli.main import dbtRunner
130	
131	    run_id = quote(run_id_raw, safe="")
132	
133	    conn_uri = os.environ["AIRFLOW_CONN_GARAGEFS"]
134	    parsed = urlparse(conn_uri)
135	    extras = {k: v[0] for k, v in parse_qs(parsed.query).items()}
136	    s3 = boto3.client(
137	        "s3",
138	        endpoint_url=extras.get("endpoint_url", "http://garage.shared.svc.cluster.local:3900"),
139	        aws_access_key_id=unquote(parsed.username or ""),
140	        aws_secret_access_key=unquote(parsed.password or ""),
141	        region_name=extras.get("region_name", "garage"),
142	    )
143	
144	    # 1. List and download all run_results shards for this DAG run.
145	    shard_prefix = f"_runs/{run_id}/run_results/"
146	    resp = s3.list_objects_v2(Bucket=s3_bucket, Prefix=shard_prefix)
147	    shard_keys = [obj["Key"] for obj in resp.get("Contents", [])]
148	    print(f"Found {len(shard_keys)} shards at s3://{s3_bucket}/{shard_prefix}")
149	    if not shard_keys:
150	        raise RuntimeError(
151	            f"No run_results shards under s3://{s3_bucket}/{shard_prefix}; "
152	            "upstream dbt tasks did not upload anything"
153	        )
154	
155	    # 2. Merge shards. Each shard's "results" array has one entry (Cosmos runs
156	    #    one dbt node per task). We concatenate results, preserve metadata/args
157	    #    from the first shard, and sum execution_time for elapsed_time.
158	    merged_results = []
159	    template = None
160	    for key in shard_keys:
161	        data = json.loads(s3.get_object(Bucket=s3_bucket, Key=key)["Body"].read())
162	        if template is None:
163	            template = data
164	        merged_results.extend(data.get("results", []))
165	    merged = {
166	        "metadata": template["metadata"],
167	        "args": template["args"],
168	        "elapsed_time": sum(r.get("execution_time", 0) for r in merged_results),
169	        "results": merged_results,
170	    }
171	
172	    # 3. Write merged run_results.json into the pod-local dbt target dir.
173	    target = Path(dbt_target_path)
174	    target.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
175	    (target / "run_results.json").write_text(json.dumps(merged))
176	    print(f"Wrote merged run_results.json with {len(merged_results)} result entries")
177	
178	    # 4. dbt docs generate — compiles the project (writes manifest.json) and
179	    #    queries Trino information_schema (writes catalog.json) into target.
180	    os.environ["DBT_TARGET_PATH"] = str(target)
181	    result = dbtRunner().invoke([
182	        "docs", "generate",
183	        "--project-dir", dbt_project_path,
184	        "--profiles-dir", dbt_project_path,
185	    ])
186	    if not result.success:
187	        raise RuntimeError(f"dbt docs generate failed: {result.exception}")
188	    print("dbt docs generate succeeded")
189	
190	    # 5. Upload canonical artifacts to the OM-watched prefix.
191	    for name in ("manifest.json", "catalog.json", "run_results.json"):
192	        local = target / name
193	        if not local.exists():
194	            raise FileNotFoundError(f"Expected {name} at {local} after dbt docs generate")
195	        s3.upload_file(str(local), s3_bucket, f"{s3_prefix}/{name}")
196	        print(f"  Uploaded {name} -> s3://{s3_bucket}/{s3_prefix}/{name}")
197	
198	    # 6. Cleanup shard prefix.
199	    s3.delete_objects(
200	        Bucket=s3_bucket,
201	        Delete={"Objects": [{"Key": k} for k in shard_keys]},
202	    )
203	    print(f"Deleted {len(shard_keys)} shards under {shard_prefix}")

206	def _om_helpers():
207	    """Return shared OpenMetadata API helper functions."""
208	    import json
209	    import urllib.request
210	    import urllib.error
211	
212	    def om_request(path, method="GET", data=None, token=None):
213	        url = f"{OM_API}{path}"
214	        headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json"}
215	        if token:
216	            headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {token}"
217	        body = json.dumps(data).encode() if data else None
218	        req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=body, headers=headers, method=method)
219	        with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as resp:
220	            return json.loads(resp.read().decode())
221	
222	    def om_login():
223	        import os
224	        import urllib.parse
225	        data = urllib.parse.urlencode({
226	            "grant_type": "password",
227	            "client_id": OM_OIDC_CLIENT_ID,
228	            "client_secret": OM_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET,
229	            "username": OM_ADMIN_USER,
230	            "password": os.environ.get("KEYCLOAK_DEMO_ADMIN_PASSWORD", ""),
231	            "scope": "openid",
232	        }).encode()
233	        req = urllib.request.Request(
234	            KEYCLOAK_TOKEN_URL, data=data,
235	            headers={"Content-Type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded"}, method="POST",
236	        )
237	        with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as resp:
238	            token = json.loads(resp.read().decode())["access_token"]
239	        print("  Obtained OpenMetadata token from Keycloak.")
240	        return token
241	
242	    return om_request, om_login

245	def trigger_om_metadata_ingestion(**context):
246	    """Trigger the OpenMetadata metadata ingestion pipeline and wait for completion."""
247	    import time
248	
249	    om_request, om_login = _om_helpers()
250	    token = om_login()
251	
252	    # Look up metadata ingestion pipeline by FQN
253	    pipeline = om_request(
254	        f"/services/ingestionPipelines/name/{METADATA_PIPELINE_FQN}", token=token
255	    )
256	    pipeline_id = pipeline["id"]
257	    print(f"  Found metadata pipeline: {METADATA_PIPELINE_FQN} (id={pipeline_id})")
258	
259	    # Record start time before triggering (milliseconds for OM API)
260	    trigger_ts = int(time.time() * 1000)
261	
262	    # Trigger the pipeline
263	    om_request(
264	        f"/services/ingestionPipelines/trigger/{pipeline_id}",
265	        method="POST",
266	        token=token,
267	    )
268	    print("  Metadata ingestion triggered. Waiting for completion...")
269	
270	    # Poll for completion
271	    elapsed = 0
272	    while elapsed < INGESTION_TIMEOUT:
273	        time.sleep(INGESTION_POLL_INTERVAL)
274	        elapsed += INGESTION_POLL_INTERVAL
275	
276	        try:
277	            # Refresh the token each poll: Keycloak access tokens expire (~300s by
278	            # default), which is shorter than INGESTION_TIMEOUT, so a single token
279	            # would die mid-loop on a slow ingestion.
280	            token = om_login()
281	            now_ts = int(time.time() * 1000)
282	            status_resp = om_request(
283	                f"/services/ingestionPipelines/{METADATA_PIPELINE_FQN}/pipelineStatus"
284	                f"?startTs={trigger_ts}&endTs={now_ts}",
285	                token=token,
286	            )
287	        except Exception as e:
288	            print(f"  [{elapsed}s] Status check failed ({e}), will retry...")
289	            continue
290	
291	        # ResultList<PipelineStatus>: {"data": [...], "paging": {...}}
292	        statuses = status_resp.get("data", [])
293	        if not statuses:
294	            print(f"  [{elapsed}s] No status available yet...")
295	            continue
296	
297	        latest = statuses[0]
298	        state = latest.get("pipelineState", "unknown")
299	        print(f"  [{elapsed}s] Pipeline state: {state}")
300	
301	        if state in ("success", "partialSuccess"):
302	            print("  Metadata ingestion completed successfully.")
303	            return
304	        elif state in ("failed", "error"):
305	            raise RuntimeError(
306	                f"Metadata ingestion pipeline failed with state: {state}"
307	            )
308	
309	    raise TimeoutError(
310	        f"Metadata ingestion did not complete within {INGESTION_TIMEOUT}s"
311	    )

329	        print(f"  Warning: Could not trigger dbt ingestion: {e}")
330	        print("  The pipeline will run on its schedule or can be triggered from the OpenMetadata UI.")
331	
332	
333	with DAG(
334	    dag_id="dbt_tpch_demo",
335	    schedule="@once",
336	    start_date=datetime(2024, 1, 1),
337	    catchup=False,
338	    is_paused_upon_creation=False,
339	    default_args={"retries": 1000},
340	) as dag:
341	
342	    wait_for_services = PythonSensor(
343	        task_id="wait_for_services",
344	        python_callable=check_services_ready,
345	        poke_interval=60,
346	        # OpenMetadata (+ its OpenSearch index/migrations) and the trino-init
347	        # schema job can take 15-25 min on a cold cluster, and this @once DAG
348	        # fires early in bring-up. 15 min was too short -> the whole pipeline
349	        # failed on first deploy with no auto-recovery. Give it 40 min.
350	        timeout=2400,
351	        # reschedule: release the KubernetesExecutor pod between pokes instead of
352	        # blocking a slot for up to 40 min while waiting.
353	        mode="reschedule",
354	    )
355	
356	    dbt_tasks = DbtTaskGroup(
357	        group_id="dbt_tpch",
358	        project_config=ProjectConfig(
359	            dbt_project_path=DBT_PROJECT_PATH,
360	        ),
361	        profile_config=ProfileConfig(
362	            profiles_yml_filepath=DBT_PROJECT_PATH / "profiles.yml",
363	            profile_name="tpch_demo",
364	            target_name="dev",
365	        ),
366	        render_config=RenderConfig(
367	            load_method=LoadMode.CUSTOM,
368	        ),
369	        execution_config=ExecutionConfig(
370	            execution_mode=ExecutionMode.VIRTUALENV,
371	            virtualenv_dir=Path("/tmp/dbt_venv"),
372	        ),
373	        operator_args={
374	            "py_system_site_packages": False,
375	            "py_requirements": ["dbt-trino"],
376	            "install_deps": True,
377	            # Cosmos VIRTUALENV runs dbt in a subprocess that does NOT inherit the
378	            # task pod's environment by default, so profiles.yml's
379	            # env_var('TRINO_PASSWORD') resolved empty -> dbt sent admin:"" and
380	            # Trino returned 401. append_env merges the task env (which carries
381	            # TRINO_PASSWORD from the executor podOverride) into the dbt subprocess.
382	            "append_env": True,
383	        },
384	        default_args={
385	            "retries": 1,
386	            "on_success_callback": upload_run_results_shard,
387	            "on_failure_callback": upload_run_results_shard,
388	        },
389	    )
390	
391	    finalize = PythonVirtualenvOperator(
392	        task_id="finalize_dbt_artifacts",
393	        python_callable=finalize_dbt_artifacts,
394	        requirements=["dbt-trino", "boto3"],
395	        system_site_packages=False,
396	        python_version="3.12",
397	        op_kwargs={
398	            "dbt_project_path": str(DBT_PROJECT_PATH),
399	            "dbt_target_path": str(DBT_TARGET_PATH),
400	            "s3_bucket": S3_BUCKET,
401	            "s3_prefix": S3_PREFIX,
402	            "run_id_raw": "{{ dag_run.run_id }}",
403	        },
404	    )
405	
406	    trigger_metadata_ingestion = PythonOperator(
407	        task_id="trigger_om_metadata_ingestion",
408	        python_callable=trigger_om_metadata_ingestion,
409	    )
410	
411	    trigger_dbt_ingestion = PythonOperator(
412	        task_id="trigger_om_dbt_ingestion",
413	        python_callable=trigger_om_dbt_ingestion,
414	    )

# This file is an airflow DAG definition using Astronomer Cosmos for dbt orchestration.
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path

from airflow import DAG
from airflow.operators.python import PythonOperator, PythonVirtualenvOperator
from airflow.sensors.python import PythonSensor
from cosmos import DbtTaskGroup, ProjectConfig, ProfileConfig, ExecutionConfig, RenderConfig
from cosmos.constants import ExecutionMode, LoadMode

DBT_PROJECT_PATH = Path("/stackable/app/git-0/current/dags/dbt/tpch_demo")
DBT_TARGET_PATH = Path("/tmp/dbt-target")
S3_BUCKET = "dbt-artifacts"
S3_PREFIX = "tpch_demo"
OM_HOST = "http://openmetadata:8585"
OM_API = f"{OM_HOST}/api/v1"
# OM runs in custom-oidc mode, so basic /users/login is forbidden. We get a
# bearer token from Keycloak (demo-admin password grant via the openmetadata
# client -> aud=openmetadata, accepted by OM). Password is injected into the
# executor pod as KEYCLOAK_DEMO_ADMIN_PASSWORD (see the AirflowCluster).
KEYCLOAK_TOKEN_URL = "http://keycloak-service.platform.svc.cluster.local:8080/realms/stackable-demo/protocol/openid-connect/token"
OM_OIDC_CLIENT_ID = "openmetadata"
OM_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET = "openmetadata-secret"
OM_ADMIN_USER = "demo-admin"
METADATA_PIPELINE_FQN = "trino.trino_metadata_ingestion"
DBT_PIPELINE_FQN = "trino.trino_dbt_ingestion"
INGESTION_POLL_INTERVAL = 10  # seconds
INGESTION_TIMEOUT = 600  # seconds

TRINO_SCHEMA_CHECK = "hive-iceberg.demo"


def check_services_ready(**context):
    """Check that OpenMetadata API is responding and Trino has the required schema."""
    import urllib.request
    import urllib.error

    # --- Check OpenMetadata health ---
    try:
        req = urllib.request.Request(f"{OM_HOST}/api/v1/system/version")
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=10) as resp:
            resp.read()
        print("  OpenMetadata API is reachable.")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"  OpenMetadata not ready: {e}")
        return False

    # --- Check Trino schema via Airflow TrinoHook ---
    try:
        from airflow.providers.trino.hooks.trino import TrinoHook

        catalog, schema = TRINO_SCHEMA_CHECK.split(".", 1)
        hook = TrinoHook(trino_conn_id="trino_default")
        records = hook.get_records(f"SHOW SCHEMAS FROM \"{catalog}\" LIKE '{schema}'")
        if any(row[0] == schema for row in records):
            print(f"  Trino schema {TRINO_SCHEMA_CHECK} exists.")
        else:
            print(f"  Trino is up but schema {TRINO_SCHEMA_CHECK} not found yet.")
            return False
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"  Trino not ready: {e}")
        return False

    print("  All services are ready.")
    return True


def upload_run_results_shard(context):
    """Upload this task's run_results.json shard to GarageFS after dbt execution.

    Runs as the Airflow on_success_callback / on_failure_callback for each
    Cosmos-generated dbt task. Failed tasks often still produce a valid
    run_results.json (e.g. test failures) that OpenMetadata wants to ingest, so
    we upload on both success and failure.
    """
    import os
    from pathlib import Path
    from urllib.parse import quote
    import boto3
    from airflow.hooks.base import BaseHook

    target_dir = Path(os.environ.get("DBT_TARGET_PATH", "/tmp/dbt-target"))
    local = target_dir / "run_results.json"
    if not local.exists():
        print(f"  No run_results.json at {local}; nothing to upload")
        return

    run_id = quote(context["dag_run"].run_id, safe="")
    task_id = context["ti"].task_id
    key = f"_runs/{run_id}/run_results/{task_id}.json"

    conn = BaseHook.get_connection("garagefs")
    extras = conn.extra_dejson
    s3 = boto3.client(
        "s3",
        endpoint_url=extras.get("endpoint_url", "http://garage.shared.svc.cluster.local:3900"),
        aws_access_key_id=conn.login,
        aws_secret_access_key=conn.password,
        region_name=extras.get("region_name", "garage"),
    )
    s3.upload_file(str(local), S3_BUCKET, key)
    print(f"  Uploaded run_results shard -> s3://{S3_BUCKET}/{key}")


def finalize_dbt_artifacts(
    dbt_project_path: str,
    dbt_target_path: str,
    s3_bucket: str,
    s3_prefix: str,
    run_id_raw: str,
):
    """Merge per-task run_results shards, regenerate manifest+catalog via
    dbt docs generate, publish all three canonical artifacts to S3, and delete
    the shard prefix.

    Runs inside a PythonVirtualenvOperator with dbt-trino + boto3 installed
    into the venv. Fully self-contained — imports live inside the body because
    the callable is serialized into a subprocess, and we avoid `airflow.*`
    imports entirely because uv's venv doesn't inherit the Stackable Airflow
    image's site-packages reliably. The garagefs connection is read straight
    from the AIRFLOW_CONN_GARAGEFS env var (which Airflow sets on executor
    pods from the garagefs-airflow-credentials secret).
    """
    import json
    import os
    from pathlib import Path
    from urllib.parse import quote, urlparse, parse_qs, unquote
    import boto3
    from dbt.cli.main import dbtRunner

    run_id = quote(run_id_raw, safe="")

    conn_uri = os.environ["AIRFLOW_CONN_GARAGEFS"]
    parsed = urlparse(conn_uri)
    extras = {k: v[0] for k, v in parse_qs(parsed.query).items()}
    s3 = boto3.client(
        "s3",
        endpoint_url=extras.get("endpoint_url", "http://garage.shared.svc.cluster.local:3900"),
        aws_access_key_id=unquote(parsed.username or ""),
        aws_secret_access_key=unquote(parsed.password or ""),
        region_name=extras.get("region_name", "garage"),
    )

    # 1. List and download all run_results shards for this DAG run.
    shard_prefix = f"_runs/{run_id}/run_results/"
    resp = s3.list_objects_v2(Bucket=s3_bucket, Prefix=shard_prefix)
    shard_keys = [obj["Key"] for obj in resp.get("Contents", [])]
    print(f"Found {len(shard_keys)} shards at s3://{s3_bucket}/{shard_prefix}")
    if not shard_keys:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"No run_results shards under s3://{s3_bucket}/{shard_prefix}; "
            "upstream dbt tasks did not upload anything"
        )

    # 2. Merge shards. Each shard's "results" array has one entry (Cosmos runs
    #    one dbt node per task). We concatenate results, preserve metadata/args
    #    from the first shard, and sum execution_time for elapsed_time.
    merged_results = []
    template = None
    for key in shard_keys:
        data = json.loads(s3.get_object(Bucket=s3_bucket, Key=key)["Body"].read())
        if template is None:
            template = data
        merged_results.extend(data.get("results", []))
    merged = {
        "metadata": template["metadata"],
        "args": template["args"],
        "elapsed_time": sum(r.get("execution_time", 0) for r in merged_results),
        "results": merged_results,
    }

    # 3. Write merged run_results.json into the pod-local dbt target dir.
    target = Path(dbt_target_path)
    target.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (target / "run_results.json").write_text(json.dumps(merged))
    print(f"Wrote merged run_results.json with {len(merged_results)} result entries")

    # 4. dbt docs generate — compiles the project (writes manifest.json) and
    #    queries Trino information_schema (writes catalog.json) into target.
    os.environ["DBT_TARGET_PATH"] = str(target)
    result = dbtRunner().invoke([
        "docs", "generate",
        "--project-dir", dbt_project_path,
        "--profiles-dir", dbt_project_path,
    ])
    if not result.success:
        raise RuntimeError(f"dbt docs generate failed: {result.exception}")
    print("dbt docs generate succeeded")

    # 5. Upload canonical artifacts to the OM-watched prefix.
    for name in ("manifest.json", "catalog.json", "run_results.json"):
        local = target / name
        if not local.exists():
            raise FileNotFoundError(f"Expected {name} at {local} after dbt docs generate")
        s3.upload_file(str(local), s3_bucket, f"{s3_prefix}/{name}")
        print(f"  Uploaded {name} -> s3://{s3_bucket}/{s3_prefix}/{name}")

    # 6. Cleanup shard prefix.
    s3.delete_objects(
        Bucket=s3_bucket,
        Delete={"Objects": [{"Key": k} for k in shard_keys]},
    )
    print(f"Deleted {len(shard_keys)} shards under {shard_prefix}")


def _om_helpers():
    """Return shared OpenMetadata API helper functions."""
    import json
    import urllib.request
    import urllib.error

    def om_request(path, method="GET", data=None, token=None):
        url = f"{OM_API}{path}"
        headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json"}
        if token:
            headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {token}"
        body = json.dumps(data).encode() if data else None
        req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=body, headers=headers, method=method)
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as resp:
            return json.loads(resp.read().decode())

    def om_login():
        import os
        import urllib.parse
        data = urllib.parse.urlencode({
            "grant_type": "password",
            "client_id": OM_OIDC_CLIENT_ID,
            "client_secret": OM_OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET,
            "username": OM_ADMIN_USER,
            "password": os.environ.get("KEYCLOAK_DEMO_ADMIN_PASSWORD", ""),
            "scope": "openid",
        }).encode()
        req = urllib.request.Request(
            KEYCLOAK_TOKEN_URL, data=data,
            headers={"Content-Type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded"}, method="POST",
        )
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as resp:
            token = json.loads(resp.read().decode())["access_token"]
        print("  Obtained OpenMetadata token from Keycloak.")
        return token

    return om_request, om_login


def trigger_om_metadata_ingestion(**context):
    """Trigger the OpenMetadata metadata ingestion pipeline and wait for completion."""
    import time

    om_request, om_login = _om_helpers()
    token = om_login()

    # Look up metadata ingestion pipeline by FQN
    pipeline = om_request(
        f"/services/ingestionPipelines/name/{METADATA_PIPELINE_FQN}", token=token
    )
    pipeline_id = pipeline["id"]
    print(f"  Found metadata pipeline: {METADATA_PIPELINE_FQN} (id={pipeline_id})")

    # Record start time before triggering (milliseconds for OM API)
    trigger_ts = int(time.time() * 1000)

    # Trigger the pipeline
    om_request(
        f"/services/ingestionPipelines/trigger/{pipeline_id}",
        method="POST",
        token=token,
    )
    print("  Metadata ingestion triggered. Waiting for completion...")

    # Poll for completion
    elapsed = 0
    while elapsed < INGESTION_TIMEOUT:
        time.sleep(INGESTION_POLL_INTERVAL)
        elapsed += INGESTION_POLL_INTERVAL

        try:
            # Refresh the token each poll: Keycloak access tokens expire (~300s by
            # default), which is shorter than INGESTION_TIMEOUT, so a single token
            # would die mid-loop on a slow ingestion.
            token = om_login()
            now_ts = int(time.time() * 1000)
            status_resp = om_request(
                f"/services/ingestionPipelines/{METADATA_PIPELINE_FQN}/pipelineStatus"
                f"?startTs={trigger_ts}&endTs={now_ts}",
                token=token,
            )
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"  [{elapsed}s] Status check failed ({e}), will retry...")
            continue

        # ResultList<PipelineStatus>: {"data": [...], "paging": {...}}
        statuses = status_resp.get("data", [])
        if not statuses:
            print(f"  [{elapsed}s] No status available yet...")
            continue

        latest = statuses[0]
        state = latest.get("pipelineState", "unknown")
        print(f"  [{elapsed}s] Pipeline state: {state}")

        if state in ("success", "partialSuccess"):
            print("  Metadata ingestion completed successfully.")
            return
        elif state in ("failed", "error"):
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"Metadata ingestion pipeline failed with state: {state}"
            )

    raise TimeoutError(
        f"Metadata ingestion did not complete within {INGESTION_TIMEOUT}s"
    )


def trigger_om_dbt_ingestion(**context):
    """Trigger the OpenMetadata dbt ingestion pipeline via REST API."""
    om_request, om_login = _om_helpers()
    token = om_login()

    # Look up pipeline by FQN
    pipeline = om_request(f"/services/ingestionPipelines/name/{DBT_PIPELINE_FQN}", token=token)
    pipeline_id = pipeline["id"]
    print(f"  Found dbt pipeline: {DBT_PIPELINE_FQN} (id={pipeline_id})")

    # Trigger
    try:
        om_request(f"/services/ingestionPipelines/trigger/{pipeline_id}", method="POST", token=token)
        print("  dbt ingestion triggered successfully.")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"  Warning: Could not trigger dbt ingestion: {e}")
        print("  The pipeline will run on its schedule or can be triggered from the OpenMetadata UI.")


with DAG(
    dag_id="dbt_tpch_demo",
    schedule="@once",
    start_date=datetime(2024, 1, 1),
    catchup=False,
    is_paused_upon_creation=False,
    default_args={"retries": 1000},
) as dag:

    wait_for_services = PythonSensor(
        task_id="wait_for_services",
        python_callable=check_services_ready,
        poke_interval=60,
        # OpenMetadata (+ its OpenSearch index/migrations) and the trino-init
        # schema job can take 15-25 min on a cold cluster, and this @once DAG
        # fires early in bring-up. 15 min was too short -> the whole pipeline
        # failed on first deploy with no auto-recovery. Give it 40 min.
        timeout=2400,
        # reschedule: release the KubernetesExecutor pod between pokes instead of
        # blocking a slot for up to 40 min while waiting.
        mode="reschedule",
    )

    dbt_tasks = DbtTaskGroup(
        group_id="dbt_tpch",
        project_config=ProjectConfig(
            dbt_project_path=DBT_PROJECT_PATH,
        ),
        profile_config=ProfileConfig(
            profiles_yml_filepath=DBT_PROJECT_PATH / "profiles.yml",
            profile_name="tpch_demo",
            target_name="dev",
        ),
        render_config=RenderConfig(
            load_method=LoadMode.CUSTOM,
        ),
        execution_config=ExecutionConfig(
            execution_mode=ExecutionMode.VIRTUALENV,
            virtualenv_dir=Path("/tmp/dbt_venv"),
        ),
        operator_args={
            "py_system_site_packages": False,
            "py_requirements": ["dbt-trino"],
            "install_deps": True,
            # Cosmos VIRTUALENV runs dbt in a subprocess that does NOT inherit the
            # task pod's environment by default, so profiles.yml's
            # env_var('TRINO_PASSWORD') resolved empty -> dbt sent admin:"" and
            # Trino returned 401. append_env merges the task env (which carries
            # TRINO_PASSWORD from the executor podOverride) into the dbt subprocess.
            "append_env": True,
        },
        default_args={
            "retries": 1,
            "on_success_callback": upload_run_results_shard,
            "on_failure_callback": upload_run_results_shard,
        },
    )

    finalize = PythonVirtualenvOperator(
        task_id="finalize_dbt_artifacts",
        python_callable=finalize_dbt_artifacts,
        requirements=["dbt-trino", "boto3"],
        system_site_packages=False,
        python_version="3.12",
        op_kwargs={
            "dbt_project_path": str(DBT_PROJECT_PATH),
            "dbt_target_path": str(DBT_TARGET_PATH),
            "s3_bucket": S3_BUCKET,
            "s3_prefix": S3_PREFIX,
            "run_id_raw": "{{ dag_run.run_id }}",
        },
    )

    trigger_metadata_ingestion = PythonOperator(
        task_id="trigger_om_metadata_ingestion",
        python_callable=trigger_om_metadata_ingestion,
    )

    trigger_dbt_ingestion = PythonOperator(
        task_id="trigger_om_dbt_ingestion",
        python_callable=trigger_om_dbt_ingestion,
    )

    wait_for_services >> dbt_tasks >> finalize >> trigger_metadata_ingestion >> trigger_dbt_ingestion
name: tpch_demo
version: "1.0.0"
config-version: 2

profile: tpch_demo

model-paths: ["models"]
target-path: "target"
clean-targets:
  - "target"
  - "dbt_packages"

models:
  tpch_demo:
    staging:
      +materialized: view
    marts:
      +materialized: table
tpch_demo:
  target: dev
  outputs:
    dev:
      type: trino
      # LDAP = HTTP basic auth, validated by Trino's PASSWORD authenticator
      # (trino-users static auth). Password comes from the TRINO_PASSWORD env
      # injected into the executor pod from the trino-users Secret.
      method: ldap
      host: trino-coordinator
      port: 8443
      user: admin
      password: "{{ env_var('TRINO_PASSWORD') }}"
      schema: demo
      catalog: hive-iceberg
      http_scheme: https
      ssl_verify: false
      session_properties:
        query_max_run_time: 5mversion: 2

sources:
  - name: tpch
    database: tpch
    schema: tiny
    description: "TPC-H benchmark dataset (scale factor tiny) served by the Trino tpch catalog. Contains 8 tables modeling a parts supplier business with customers, orders, line items, parts, suppliers, nations, and regions."

    tables:
      - name: region
        description: Geographic regions (5 rows). Top-level grouping for nations.
        columns:
          - name: regionkey
            description: Unique region identifier (surrogate key).
          - name: name
            description: Region name (e.g. AFRICA, AMERICA, ASIA, EUROPE, MIDDLE EAST).
          - name: comment
            description: Free-text comment about the region.

      - name: nation
        description: Nations within regions (25 rows). Each nation belongs to one region.
        columns:
          - name: nationkey
            description: Unique nation identifier (surrogate key).
          - name: name
            description: Nation name (e.g. UNITED STATES, GERMANY, CHINA).
          - name: regionkey
            description: Foreign key to region.
          - name: comment
            description: Free-text comment about the nation.

      - name: supplier
        description: Parts suppliers (100 rows at tiny scale). Each supplier is in one nation.
        columns:
          - name: suppkey
            description: Unique supplier identifier (surrogate key).
          - name: name
            description: Supplier name (format Supplier#NNNNNNNNN).
          - name: address
            description: Street address of the supplier.
          - name: nationkey
            description: Foreign key to nation.
          - name: phone
            description: Phone number (format NN-NNN-NNN-NNNN).
          - name: acctbal
            description: Account balance in dollars.
          - name: comment
            description: Free-text comment about the supplier.

      - name: part
        description: Parts catalog (2,000 rows at tiny scale).
        columns:
          - name: partkey
            description: Unique part identifier (surrogate key).
          - name: name
            description: Part name composed of randomly generated words.
          - name: mfgr
            description: Manufacturer name (format Manufacturer#N).
          - name: brand
            description: Brand name (format Brand#NN).
          - name: type
            description: Part type as a 3-word compound (e.g. STANDARD POLISHED BRASS).
          - name: size
            description: Part size as an integer from 1 to 50.
          - name: container
            description: Shipping container type (e.g. SM CASE, LG BOX, MED PKG).
          - name: retailprice
            description: Retail price in dollars.
          - name: comment
            description: Free-text comment about the part.

      - name: partsupp
        description: "Part-supplier relationships (8,000 rows at tiny scale). Maps which suppliers provide which parts, with cost and availability."
        columns:
          - name: partkey
            description: Foreign key to part.
          - name: suppkey
            description: Foreign key to supplier.
          - name: availqty
            description: Number of units available from this supplier for this part.
          - name: supplycost
            description: Cost per unit from this supplier, in dollars.
          - name: comment
            description: Free-text comment about this part-supplier relationship.

      - name: customer
        description: Customers (1,500 rows at tiny scale). Each customer belongs to one nation.
        columns:
          - name: custkey
            description: Unique customer identifier (surrogate key).
          - name: name
            description: Customer name (format Customer#NNNNNNNNN).
          - name: address
            description: Street address of the customer.
          - name: nationkey
            description: Foreign key to nation.
          - name: phone
            description: Phone number (format NN-NNN-NNN-NNNN).
          - name: acctbal
            description: Account balance in dollars. May be negative.
          - name: mktsegment
            description: "Market segment (AUTOMOBILE, BUILDING, FURNITURE, HOUSEHOLD, MACHINERY)."
          - name: comment
            description: Free-text comment about the customer.

      - name: orders
        description: Customer orders (15,000 rows at tiny scale). Each order belongs to one customer.
        columns:
          - name: orderkey
            description: Unique order identifier (surrogate key).
          - name: custkey
            description: Foreign key to customer.
          - name: orderstatus
            description: "Order status: F = fulfilled, O = open, P = partially fulfilled."
          - name: totalprice
            description: Total order price in dollars.
          - name: orderdate
            description: Date the order was placed.
          - name: orderpriority
            description: "Priority level: 1-URGENT, 2-HIGH, 3-MEDIUM, 4-NOT SPECIFIED, 5-LOW."
          - name: clerk
            description: Clerk who processed the order (format Clerk#NNNNNNNNN).
          - name: shippriority
            description: Shipping priority flag (integer).
          - name: comment
            description: Free-text comment about the order.

      - name: lineitem
        description: "Order line items (60,175 rows at tiny scale). Each line item is one part on one order, supplied by one supplier. The most granular fact table."
        columns:
          - name: orderkey
            description: Foreign key to orders.
          - name: linenumber
            description: Line number within the order (1-based).
          - name: partkey
            description: Foreign key to part.
          - name: suppkey
            description: Foreign key to supplier.
          - name: quantity
            description: Quantity ordered (1 to 50).
          - name: extendedprice
            description: Line item price before discount (quantity * retail price).
          - name: discount
            description: Discount percentage as a decimal (0.00 to 0.10).
          - name: tax
            description: Tax rate as a decimal (0.00 to 0.08).
          - name: returnflag
            description: "Return status: R = returned, A = accepted, N = not yet received."
          - name: linestatus
            description: "Shipping status: F = shipped, O = not yet shipped."
          - name: shipdate
            description: Date the line item was shipped.
          - name: commitdate
            description: Committed delivery date.
          - name: receiptdate
            description: Actual date the customer received the item.
          - name: shipinstruct
            description: Shipping instruction (DELIVER IN PERSON, COLLECT COD, TAKE BACK RETURN, NONE).
          - name: shipmode
            description: Shipping mode (AIR, FOB, MAIL, RAIL, REG AIR, SHIP, TRUCK).
          - name: comment
            description: Free-text comment about the line item.

    sum(li.extended_price * (1 - li.discount))

    count(li.line_number) as total_line_items,
    count(distinct li.part_id) as distinct_parts_ordered,
    count(distinct li.supplier_id) as distinct_suppliers_used
from {{ ref('stg_customers') }} c
join {{ ref('stg_nations') }} n on c.nation_id = n.nation_id
join {{ ref('stg_regions') }} r on n.region_id = r.region_id
left join {{ ref('stg_orders') }} o on c.customer_id = o.customer_id
left join {{ ref('stg_line_items') }} li on o.order_id = li.order_id
group by

    c.market_segment,

    avg(date_diff('day', li.ship_date, li.receipt_date)) as avg_delivery_days,
    avg(date_diff('day', li.commit_date, li.receipt_date)) as avg_receipt_vs_commit_days,

        / count(*) as late_delivery_rate,
    sum(case when li.return_flag = 'R' then 1 else 0 end) as returned_items,

content.text:
I've read through the directory and taken a read-only look at the cluster. One thing first: **I caused a scheduler restart.** I ran the `airflow` CLI inside `airflow-scheduler-default-0` to check task states. The scheduler runs at about 810 Mi of its 1 Gi limit, the CLI pushed it over, and the container was OOM-killed. It came back on its own (restarts=1). I won't run the CLI in there again; I'll use the web UI/API or a separate pod instead.

## What's in the directory

- **`tpch_dbt_dag.py`**: an Apache Airflow DAG `dbt_tpch_demo`, scheduled `@once`, using Astronomer Cosmos. It runs these steps in order:
  1. `wait_for_services`: a sensor that waits until OpenMetadata answers and Trino has the `hive-iceberg.demo` schema. It checks every 60 s, gives up after 40 min, and releases its pod between checks.
  2. `dbt_tpch`: a Cosmos task group with one Airflow task per dbt model. Each runs dbt in a throwaway Python environment. After each task, its `run_results.json` is uploaded to the Garage S3 bucket `dbt-artifacts` under `_runs/<run_id>/`.
  3. `finalize_dbt_artifacts`: merges those per-task results, runs `dbt docs generate`, and publishes `manifest.json`, `catalog.json` and `run_results.json` to `s3://dbt-artifacts/tpch_demo/`.
  4. `trigger_om_metadata_ingestion` then `trigger_om_dbt_ingestion`: gets a token from Keycloak (`demo-admin` login), then starts the two OpenMetadata ingestion pipelines.
- **`dbt/tpch_demo`**: 8 staging views over Trino's `tpch.tiny` and 6 tables built from them, written to `hive-iceberg.demo`. It logs into Trino on port 8443 as `admin` with basic auth; the password comes from the `TRINO_PASSWORD` environment variable.
- **`kubeconfig`**: two AKS clusters, `data3day` and `data5day`. The current one is `data5day`, and that's the one I looked at.

## Cluster state (`data5day`, namespace `platform`)

The whole stack is up: Airflow, Trino, OpenMetadata, Keycloak, Garage, Hive, Kafka, NiFi and Superset. The one-off setup jobs (`trino-init`, `configure-openmetadata`, etc.) all completed.

**Main problem: the DAG is stuck because no node has room for its task pods.**
- The first sensor checks ran about 45 min ago. The current one, `dbt-tpch-demo-wait-for-services-7s6x6fdu`, has been Pending for about 5 min with `0/4 nodes are available: 4 Insufficient cpu`.
- Each Airflow task pod asks for 1.25 CPU and about 3.1 Gi. The three worker nodes already have 87–99 % of their CPU reserved. Real usage is only about 4 %, so this is about reservations, not load.
- The biggest reservations are the Trino workers, OpenSearch, and every Airflow component at 0.85 CPU or more each.
- Every dbt model needs its own 1.25-CPU pod, so even if the sensor gets through, the dbt step will crawl or stall.
- The sensor's 40-min limit is counted from its first check, which was about 46 min ago. So it has probably already run out or is about to, and will then burn through its retries.

**Minor:** one OPA pod (`opa-server-default-wntdd`) is Pending because it's pinned to the small system node, which is out of CPU. That's probably harmless for the demo.

## Ways to unblock it
1. **Shrink what each task pod asks for.** Set `kubernetesExecutors.config.resources` on the AirflowCluster (it's currently empty, so the operator's defaults apply), e.g. 250m CPU / 1 Gi. This is the real fix for the demo definition.
2. **Free up CPU reservations** elsewhere, e.g. NiFi, Kafka or Superset if this demo doesn't need them, or scale Trino down to one worker.
3. **Add a node** to the user pool.

Then clear or re-trigger the `dbt_tpch_demo` run.

I haven't changed anything except the accidental restart. Tell me which option you want and I'll make the change. ArgoCD and Forgejo are running in `deployment`, so a manual edit is probably reverted from Git and the fix belongs in the repo they sync from. Before applying anything I'll check whether ArgoCD manages the AirflowCluster.

**Secret exposure:** while checking the kubeconfig structure I printed the start of the static `token:` values for both users (lines 27 and 32 of `kubeconfig`). They're now in this session's transcript. Note that file also holds full admin client certificates for both clusters. If these clusters are meant to last longer than a demo, rotate the credentials.

content.text:
I made the three changes and committed them locally. Nothing was deployed or pushed.

The specs weren't on this machine, so I cloned the repo ArgoCD deploys from: the in-cluster Forgejo repo `stackable/openmetadata-dbt-demo`, branch `feat/data2day`. The clone is at `/workspace/openmetadata-dbt-demo`.

Commit `afd2df1` ("Free cluster CPU: stop NiFi, scale Kafka brokers and Trino workers to 1") changes three files:
- `platform/manifests/nifi/nifi.yaml`: `clusterOperation.stopped: true`
- `platform/manifests/kafka/kafka.yaml`: brokers `replicas: 2` → `1` (I left the controllers at 3)
- `platform/manifests/trino/trino.yaml`: workers `replicas: 2` → `1`

The author is `Sönke Liebau <soenke.liebau@stackable.tech>`, copied from the repo's history. I committed with signing turned off, so you'll need to re-sign it: `git commit --amend -S --no-edit`.

**Pushing:** `origin` points at `http://localhost:3300/...`, a port-forward to Forgejo that I left running in the background. It disappears when the session ends; restart it with `kubectl -n deployment port-forward svc/forgejo-http 3300:3000`.

**After you push:**

---
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Application
metadata:
  name: openmetadata
  namespace: deployment
  annotations:
    argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "2"
spec:
  project: dbt-openmetadata-demo
  destination:
    server: https://kubernetes.default.svc
    namespace: platform
  sources:
    - repoURL: "https://open-metadata.github.io/openmetadata-helm-charts"
      chart: openmetadata
      targetRevision: "1.12.1" # renovate: registryUrl=https://open-metadata.github.io/openmetadata-helm-charts datasource=helm depName=openmetadata
      helm:
        releaseName: openmetadata
        valuesObject:
          openmetadata:
            config:
              elasticsearch:
                enabled: true
                host: simple-opensearch-nodes-default
                searchType: opensearch
                port: 9200
                scheme: https
                trustStore:
                  enabled: true
                  path: /certs-jks/truststore.jks
                  password:
                    secretRef: openmetadata-truststore-credentials
                    secretKey: openmetadata-truststore-password
                auth:
                  enabled: true
                  username: "openmetadata"
                  password:
                    secretRef: opensearch-openmetadata-credentials
                    secretKey: password
              database:
                host: postgresql-openmetadata.shared.svc.cluster.local
                port: 5432
                driverClass: org.postgresql.Driver
                dbScheme: postgresql
                databaseName: openmetadata
                auth:
                  username: openmetadata
                  password:
                    secretRef: postgresql-openmetadata
                    secretKey: openmetadata-postgresql-password
                dbParams: ""
              # No Airflow deploy step needed with the k8s pipeline client
              deployPipelinesConfig:
                enabled: false
              pipelineServiceClientConfig:
                type: "k8s"
                metadataApiEndpoint: http://openmetadata:8585/api # default value
                k8s:
                  # Container image for ingestion jobs
                  ingestionImage: "docker.getcollate.io/openmetadata/ingestion-base:1.12.1"
              authentication:
                provider: "custom-oidc"
                publicKeys:
                  - "$(ISSUER_URL)/protocol/openid-connect/certs"
                authority: "$(ISSUER_URL)"
                clientId: "openmetadata"
                callbackUrl: "http://$(NODE_IP):30585/callback"
              authorizer:
                className: "org.openmetadata.service.security.DefaultAuthorizer"
                containerRequestFilter: "org.openmetadata.service.security.JwtFilter"
                initialAdmins:
                  - "demo-admin"
                principalDomain: "stackable.demo"
          extraEnvs:
            - name: NODE_IP
              valueFrom:
                configMapKeyRef:
                  name: oidc-endpoints
                  key: node-ip
            - name: ISSUER_URL
              valueFrom:
                configMapKeyRef:
                  name: oidc-endpoints
                  key: issuer-url
            # The authentication.* values above are rendered by the chart into an
            # envFrom Secret, where Kubernetes does NOT perform $(VAR) substitution
            # — so the OIDC issuer/callback arrive as the literal "$(ISSUER_URL)"
            # and OM's JwtFilter dies with "URI is not absolute". Re-declare them
            # here as explicit env entries: env[] DOES expand $(ISSUER_URL)/$(NODE_IP)
            # (NODE_IP/ISSUER_URL are defined just above) and takes precedence over
            # envFrom, so OM receives absolute URLs.
            - name: AUTHENTICATION_AUTHORITY
              value: "$(ISSUER_URL)"
            - name: AUTHENTICATION_PUBLIC_KEYS
              value: '["$(ISSUER_URL)/protocol/openid-connect/certs"]'
            - name: AUTHENTICATION_CALLBACK_URL
              value: "http://$(NODE_IP):30585/callback"
          extraInitContainers:
            - name: convert-truststore
              image: eclipse-temurin:21-jre
              command:
                - sh
                - -c
                - |
                  keytool -importcert \
                    -file /certs-pem/ca.crt \
                    -keystore /certs-jks/truststore.jks \
                    -storetype JKS \
                    -storepass changeit \
                    -alias stackable-ca \
                    -noprompt
              volumeMounts:
                - name: ca-cert
                  mountPath: /certs-pem
                  readOnly: true
                - name: certs-jks
                  mountPath: /certs-jks
          extraVolumes:
            - name: ca-cert
              configMap:
                name: openmetadata-tls-truststore
            - name: certs-jks
              emptyDir: {}
          extraVolumeMounts:
            - name: certs-jks
              mountPath: /certs-jks
              readOnly: true
    - repoURL: "http://forgejo-http.deployment.svc.cluster.local:3000/stackable/openmetadata-dbt-demo.git"
      targetRevision: "feat/data2day"
      path: platform/manifests/openmetadata/
  syncPolicy:
    syncOptions:
      - CreateNamespace=true
    automated:
      selfHeal: true
      prune: true
      multivalued         = true
      add_to_id_token     = true
      add_to_access_token = true
      add_to_userinfo     = true
    }

    resource "keycloak_openid_client" "openmetadata" {
      realm_id              = keycloak_realm.stackable_demo.id
      client_id             = "openmetadata"
      name                  = "OpenMetadata"
      enabled               = true
      access_type           = "CONFIDENTIAL"
      client_secret         = "openmetadata-secret"
      standard_flow_enabled = true
      # Lets the configure-openmetadata job and the dbt DAG obtain a demo-admin
      # bearer token via password grant (OM is in custom-oidc mode -> no basic login).
      direct_access_grants_enabled = true
      valid_redirect_uris   = ["*"]
      web_origins           = ["+"]
    }

    resource "keycloak_openid_client_default_scopes" "openmetadata_scopes" {
      realm_id  = keycloak_realm.stackable_demo.id
      client_id = keycloak_openid_client.openmetadata.id
      default_scopes = [
        "profile",
        "email",
        "roles",
        "web-origins",
      ]
    }

    resource "keycloak_openid_audience_protocol_mapper" "openmetadata_audience" {
      realm_id                 = keycloak_realm.stackable_demo.id
      client_id                = keycloak_openid_client.openmetadata.id
      name                     = "openmetadata-audience"
      included_client_audience = "openmetadata"
      add_to_id_token          = true
      add_to_access_token      = true
    }

    resource "keycloak_openid_client" "cockpit" {
      realm_id                        = keycloak_realm.stackable_demo.id
      client_id                       = "cockpit"
      name                            = "Stackable Cockpit"
      enabled                         = true

---
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: configure-keycloak
  namespace: platform
  annotations:
    argocd.argoproj.io/sync-options: Replace=true
spec:
  ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 86400
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: opentofu
          image: oowy/opentofu:1.10.6-alpine3.20 # renovate: datasource=docker depName=oowy/opentofu
          command: ["/bin/sh", "-c"]
          args:
            - |
              echo "Waiting for Keycloak to be ready..."
              until wget -q -O /dev/null http://keycloak-service.platform.svc.cluster.local:8080/realms/master 2>/dev/null; do
                echo "  Not ready, retrying in 5s..."
                sleep 5
              done
              echo "Keycloak is ready."
              mkdir /work
              cd /work
              cp /config/keycloak.tf .
              tofu init
              tofu plan
              tofu apply -auto-approve
          env:
            - name: TF_VAR_keycloak_admin_username
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef: { name: keycloak-bootstrap-admin, key: username }
            - name: TF_VAR_keycloak_admin_password
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef: { name: keycloak-bootstrap-admin, key: password }
            - name: TF_VAR_demo_admin_password
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef: { name: keycloak-demo-passwords, key: demo_admin_password }
            - name: TF_VAR_demo_user_password
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef: { name: keycloak-demo-passwords, key: demo_user_password }
          volumeMounts:
            - mountPath: /config
              name: keycloak-configuration
      restartPolicy: Never
      volumes:
        - name: keycloak-configuration
          configMap: { name: keycloak-configuration }
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: keycloak-configuration
  namespace: platform
data:
  keycloak.tf: |
    terraform {
      required_providers {
        keycloak = {
          source  = "keycloak/keycloak"
          version = "~> 5.0"
        }
      }
    }

      password      = var.keycloak_admin_password
      url           = "http://keycloak-service.platform.svc.cluster.local:8080"
      realm         = "master"

---
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Application
metadata:
  name: openmetadata
  namespace: deployment
  annotations:
    argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave: "2"
spec:
  project: dbt-openmetadata-demo
  destination:
    server: https://kubernetes.default.svc
    namespace: platform
  sources:
    - repoURL: "https://open-metadata.github.io/openmetadata-helm-charts"
      chart: openmetadata
      targetRevision: "1.12.1" # renovate: registryUrl=https://open-metadata.github.io/openmetadata-helm-charts datasource=helm depName=openmetadata
      helm:
        releaseName: openmetadata
        valuesObject:
          openmetadata:
            config:
              elasticsearch:
                enabled: true
                host: simple-opensearch-nodes-default
                searchType: opensearch
                port: 9200
                scheme: https
                trustStore:
                  enabled: true
                  path: /certs-jks/truststore.jks
                  password:
                    secretRef: openmetadata-truststore-credentials
                    secretKey: openmetadata-truststore-password
                auth:
                  enabled: true
                  username: "openmetadata"
                  password:
                    secretRef: opensearch-openmetadata-credentials
                    secretKey: password
              database:
                host: postgresql-openmetadata.shared.svc.cluster.local
                port: 5432
                driverClass: org.postgresql.Driver
                dbScheme: postgresql
                databaseName: openmetadata
                auth:
                  username: openmetadata
                  password:
                    secretRef: postgresql-openmetadata
                    secretKey: openmetadata-postgresql-password
                dbParams: ""
              # No Airflow deploy step needed with the k8s pipeline client
              deployPipelinesConfig:
                enabled: false
              pipelineServiceClientConfig:
                type: "k8s"
                metadataApiEndpoint: http://openmetadata:8585/api # default value
                k8s:
                  # Container image for ingestion jobs
                  ingestionImage: "docker.getcollate.io/openmetadata/ingestion-base:1.12.1"
              authentication:
                provider: "custom-oidc"
                publicKeys:
                  - "$(ISSUER_URL)/protocol/openid-connect/certs"
                authority: "$(ISSUER_URL)"
                clientId: "openmetadata"
                callbackUrl: "http://$(NODE_IP):30585/callback"
              authorizer:
                className: "org.openmetadata.service.security.DefaultAuthorizer"
                containerRequestFilter: "org.openmetadata.service.security.JwtFilter"
                initialAdmins:
                  - "demo-admin"
                principalDomain: "stackable.demo"
          extraEnvs:
            - name: NODE_IP
              valueFrom:
                configMapKeyRef:
                  name: oidc-endpoints
                  key: node-ip
            - name: ISSUER_URL
              valueFrom:
                configMapKeyRef:
                  name: oidc-endpoints
                  key: issuer-url
            # The authentication.* values above are rendered by the chart into an
            # envFrom Secret, where Kubernetes does NOT perform $(VAR) substitution
            # — so the OIDC issuer/callback arrive as the literal "$(ISSUER_URL)"
            # and OM's JwtFilter dies with "URI is not absolute". Re-declare them
            # here as explicit env entries: env[] DOES expand $(ISSUER_URL)/$(NODE_IP)
            # (NODE_IP/ISSUER_URL are defined just above) and takes precedence over
            # envFrom, so OM receives absolute URLs.
            - name: AUTHENTICATION_AUTHORITY
              value: "$(ISSUER_URL)"
            - name: AUTHENTICATION_PUBLIC_KEYS
              value: '["$(ISSUER_URL)/protocol/openid-connect/certs"]'
            - name: AUTHENTICATION_CALLBACK_URL
              value: "http://$(NODE_IP):30585/callback"
          extraInitContainers:
            - name: convert-truststore
              image: eclipse-temurin:21-jre
              command:
                - sh
                - -c
                - |
                  keytool -importcert \
                    -file /certs-pem/ca.crt \
                    -keystore /certs-jks/truststore.jks \
                    -storetype JKS \
                    -storepass changeit \
                    -alias stackable-ca \
                    -noprompt
              volumeMounts:
                - name: ca-cert
                  mountPath: /certs-pem
                  readOnly: true
                - name: certs-jks
                  mountPath: /certs-jks
          extraVolumes:
            - name: ca-cert
              configMap:
                name: openmetadata-tls-truststore
            - name: certs-jks
              emptyDir: {}
          extraVolumeMounts:
            - name: certs-jks
              mountPath: /certs-jks
              readOnly: true
    - repoURL: "http://forgejo-http.deployment.svc.cluster.local:3000/stackable/openmetadata-dbt-demo.git"

      path: platform/manifests/openmetadata/

    syncOptions:
      - CreateNamespace=true
    automated:

content.text:
I've committed a fix as `c9de820` on top of the earlier commit. It isn't tested: I can't confirm it works until you push and log in.

**Cause:** the Helm values don't set `clientType` or `responseType`, so OpenMetadata falls back to its defaults: a public client using the implicit flow. The running pod confirms this with `AUTHENTICATION_CLIENT_TYPE=public` and `AUTHENTICATION_RESPONSE_TYPE=id_token`. The Keycloak `openmetadata` client only allows the authorization-code flow, so Keycloak rejects the login.

**Fix:** I switched OpenMetadata to a confidential client, so it uses the code flow and swaps the code for tokens itself. The client already exists in Keycloak with the right settings, so Keycloak needs no change. All changes are in `platform/applications/openmetadata.yaml`, added as `extraEnvs` for the same `$(VAR)` reason given in the file's existing comment:
- `AUTHENTICATION_CLIENT_TYPE=confidential`
- `OIDC_TYPE`, `OIDC_CLIENT_ID`, `OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET`
- `OIDC_DISCOVERY_URI`, `OIDC_CALLBACK`, `OIDC_SERVER_URL`, all built from `ISSUER_URL`/`NODE_IP`
- `AUTHENTICATION_PUBLIC_KEYS` now also lists OM's own `/api/v1/system/config/jwks`, which the OM docs require for this mode. The Keycloak keys stay in the list, so the dbt DAG and the `configure-openmetadata` job can keep using their Keycloak tokens.

**Why not just turn on implicit flow in Keycloak:** it's one line, but it wouldn't reach this cluster. `configure-keycloak` runs OpenTofu with local state inside a one-off Job. ArgoCD only re-runs that Job when its own spec changes, not when the ConfigMap holding the config does. Even a forced re-run would start with empty state and try to create the realm again. The implicit flow is also deprecated.

**Before pushing:**
- **Deploy:** pushing deploys this. `openmetadata` has automated sync with selfHeal on, and the app definition itself is synced by `cluster-apps`.
- **Secret:** `OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET` is written inline in the file. It's the same demo secret that's already in plain text in `configure-keycloak.yaml` and the DAG. If you'd rather not add another copy, I can switch it to a Secret reference.
- **Signing:** like before, both commits are unsigned. To sign both: `git rebase --exec 'git commit --amend --no-edit -S' origin/feat/data2day`.

**If login still fails after the rollout:**
- A Keycloak consent screen may appear. OM sends `prompt=consent` by default; setting `OIDC_PROMPT_TYPE` to `login` or `none` would stop that.
- The OM pod has to reach `ISSUER_URL` (node IP, port 30900) for the code exchange. It already does this to fetch Keycloak's keys, so it should be fine.

The pod logs (`kubectl -n platform logs deploy/openmetadata`) will show which of these, if either, is the problem.

message.content: Is there any downside to just turning on the implicit flow in keycloak? I was about to run a fresh deploy on a new cluster anyway..

content.text:
For a short-lived demo cluster, no serious downside. It's a valid choice, and since you're deploying fresh, my earlier objection that the Keycloak job won't re-run doesn't apply. The trade-offs:

1. **Wildcard redirect URIs make it a real risk.** The `openmetadata` client has `valid_redirect_uris = ["*"]`.
   - **Today (code flow):** a login link that redirects to an attacker's site only leaks an authorization code. That code is useless without the client secret.
   - **With implicit flow:** Keycloak puts the tokens themselves in the redirect, so anyone who gets a logged-in user to click such a link receives a working bearer token. The nodes have public IPs, so the cluster is reachable from outside.
   - **Mitigation:** restrict the redirect URIs to OM's callback, `http://<node-ip>:30585/callback`. That needs the node IP in the OpenTofu config, which might be awkward since it's only known at deploy time.
2. **It's deprecated.** The OAuth 2.0 Security Best Current Practice (RFC 9700) advises against the implicit flow, and OAuth 2.1 removes it. This matters for credibility if people look at how the demo is wired, less for function.
3. **Tokens live in the browser.** They arrive in the URL fragment and are readable by browser JavaScript and extensions. There are no refresh tokens, so OM renews sessions silently in the background, which can be flaky with browsers that block third-party cookies. This one probably won't bite you, since OM and Keycloak share the same IP.

On the plus side, the public client with implicit flow is OM's chart default, so it's the most commonly used path. My confidential-client change is untested.

My recommendation: if this is a throwaway demo, turn on implicit flow and tighten the redirect URIs if that's easy. If the repo is meant to be a reference setup people copy, keep the code flow.

Either way, pick one. If you go with implicit flow, drop `c9de820` before pushing (`git reset --hard afd2df1` in the clone), and I'll add `implicit_flow_enabled = true` to the Keycloak client instead. Want me to do that, and look at whether the redirect URIs can be restricted?
