content.content:
# Repository Guide

This is a GitOps-managed Kubernetes demo deploying a data platform (Trino, Hive, Airflow, HDFS, etc.) using Stackable operators and ArgoCD.

## Architecture

```
stackablectl (just deploy)
  └─> installs ArgoCD + bootstrap apps from infrastructure/stack.yaml
        └─> ArgoCD deploys infrastructure/ (Forgejo, SealedSecrets, project, cluster-apps)
              └─> Forgejo mirrors this GitHub repo into the cluster
              └─> cluster-apps.yaml watches platform/applications/ (app-of-apps pattern)
                    └─> each Application in platform/applications/ deploys its manifests
```

## Directory Structure

```
infrastructure/                    # Bootstrap: deployed by stackablectl, sets up ArgoCD + Forgejo + SealedSecrets
├── stack.yaml                     # stackablectl stack definition (entry point for `just deploy`)
├── project.yaml                   # ArgoCD AppProject definition
├── cluster-apps.yaml              # App-of-apps: watches platform/applications/
├── forgejo.yaml                   # ArgoCD Application for Forgejo (Helm + manifests)
├── sealed-secrets.yaml            # ArgoCD Application for SealedSecrets (Helm + manifests)
├── forgejo-manifests/             # Supporting manifests for Forgejo (admin secret, configure job)
└── sealed-secrets-manifests/      # SealedSecrets decryption key

platform/                          # Everything ArgoCD manages after bootstrap
├── applications/                  # ArgoCD Application definitions (one per component)
│   ├── <component>.yaml           # Points to manifests dir and/or Helm chart
│   └── ...
└── manifests/                     # Kubernetes manifests grouped by component
    ├── <component>/
    │   ├── <resource>.yaml        # Stackable CRDs, TrinoCatalogs, ZookeeperZnodes, etc.
    │   └── sealed-*.yaml          # SealedSecrets (generated, do not edit by hand)
    └── ...

secrets/                           # Plaintext Kubernetes Secrets (source of truth for sealed secrets)
└── manifests/
    └── <component>/
        └── <secret-name>.yaml     # Plain Secret, mirrors structure of platform/manifests/

dags/                              # Airflow DAG files (git-synced into Airflow pods)

justfile                           # Task runner (just deploy, just seal-secrets)
```

## Golden Rule

Never apply changes directly to the Kubernetes cluster (no `kubectl apply`, `helm install`, etc.). All changes must be committed to Git and deployed through ArgoCD. ArgoCD has `selfHeal: true` enabled, so any manual changes will be reverted automatically.

## How to Add a New Component

### 1. Stackable operator resource (e.g. new HiveCluster, TrinoCluster)

1. Create `platform/manifests/<component>/` with the CRD yaml files.
2. Create `platform/applications/<component>.yaml` — an ArgoCD Application pointing to the manifests dir:
   ```yaml
   source:
     repoURL: "http://forgejo-http.deployment.svc.cluster.local:3000/stackable/openmetadata-dbt-demo.git"
     targetRevision: "main"
     path: platform/manifests/<component>/
   ```
3. Commit and push. ArgoCD picks it up automatically via cluster-apps.

### 2. External Helm chart (e.g. Lakekeeper, GarageFS)

1. Create `platform/applications/<component>.yaml` with a Helm source:
   ```yaml
   sources:
     - repoURL: "https://<helm-repo-url>"
       chart: <chart-name>
       targetRevision: "<version>"    # optional but recommended
       helm:
         releaseName: <component>
   ```
2. Do NOT set `path:` when using `chart:` — they are mutually exclusive.

### 3. Helm chart + secrets/manifests (e.g. PostgreSQL instances)

Use multi-source — one source for the Helm chart, one for the manifests dir:
```yaml
sources:
  - repoURL: "registry-1.docker.io/bitnamicharts"
    chart: postgresql
    targetRevision: 16.6.3
    helm:
      releaseName: postgresql-<component>
      valuesObject:
        auth:
          existingSecret: <secret-name>
  - repoURL: "http://forgejo-http.deployment.svc.cluster.local:3000/stackable/openmetadata-dbt-demo.git"
    targetRevision: "main"
    path: platform/manifests/<component>/
```

### 4. Adding secrets

1. Create the plaintext Secret in `secrets/manifests/<component>/<secret-name>.yaml`.
2. Run `just seal-secrets` — this generates `platform/manifests/<component>/sealed-<secret-name>.yaml`.
3. Never edit sealed-* files by hand. Always edit the plaintext in `secrets/` and re-seal.

## Namespace Layout

| Namespace | Components |
|---|---|
| `deployment` | ArgoCD, SealedSecrets, Forgejo |
| `stackable-operators` | Stackable operators |
| `shared` | GarageFS, all PostgreSQL instances (airflow, hive, hive-iceberg, openmetadata, superset) |
| `platform` | Airflow, Trino, Hive, HDFS, ZooKeeper, Kafka, NiFi, OpenMetadata, OpenSearch, Superset, Lakekeeper, all init jobs |

Cross-namespace service references must use FQDNs (`<svc>.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local`).
Services within the same namespace can use short names.

## Common ArgoCD Application Fields

All applications should use:
- `project: dbt-openmetadata-demo` (except infrastructure-level apps which use `default`)
- `destination.server: https://kubernetes.default.svc`
- `destination.namespace`: `shared`, `platform`, or `deployment` depending on component (see Namespace Layout)
- `syncPolicy.automated.selfHeal: true` and `prune: true`
- `syncPolicy.syncOptions: [CreateNamespace=true]`
- `source.repoURL`: use `http://forgejo-http.deployment.svc.cluster.local:3000/stackable/openmetadata-dbt-demo.git` for Forgejo sources

## Commands

- `just deploy` — bootstrap the cluster with stackablectl (installs ArgoCD, Forgejo, then ArgoCD takes over)
- `just seal-secrets` — re-seal all plaintext secrets from `secrets/` into `platform/manifests/`

       chart: <chart-name>
       targetRevision: "<version>"    # optional but recommended
       helm:
         releaseName: <component>
   ```
2. Do NOT set `path:` when using `chart:` — they are mutually exclusive.

### 3. Helm chart + secrets/manifests (e.g. PostgreSQL instances)

Use multi-source — one source for the Helm chart, one for the manifests dir:
```yaml
sources:
  - repoURL: "registry-1.docker.io/bitnamicharts"
    chart: postgresql
    targetRevision: 16.6.3
    helm:
      releaseName: postgresql-<component>
      valuesObject:
        auth:
          existingSecret: <secret-name>
  - repoURL: "http://forgejo-http.deployment.svc.cluster.local:3000/stackable/openmetadata-dbt-demo.git"
    targetRevision: "main"
    path: platform/manifests/<component>/
```

### 4. Adding secrets

1. Create the plaintext Secret in `secrets/manifests/<component>/<secret-name>.yaml`.
2. Run `just seal-secrets` — this generates `platform/manifests/<component>/sealed-<secret-name>.yaml`.
3. Never edit sealed-* files by hand. Always edit the plaintext in `secrets/` and re-seal.

## Namespace Layout

| Namespace | Components |
|---|---|
| `deployment` | ArgoCD, SealedSecrets, Forgejo |
| `stackable-operators` | Stackable operators |
| `shared` | GarageFS, all PostgreSQL instances (airflow, hive, hive-iceberg, openmetadata, superset) |
| `platform` | Airflow, Trino, Hive, HDFS, ZooKeeper, Kafka, NiFi, OpenMetadata, OpenSearch, Superset, Lakekeeper, all init jobs |

Cross-namespace service references must use FQDNs (`<svc>.<namespace>.svc.cluster.local`).
Services within the same namespace can use short names.

## Common ArgoCD Application Fields

All applications should use:
- `project: dbt-openmetadata-demo` (except infrastructure-level apps which use `default`)
- `destination.server: https://kubernetes.default.svc`
- `destination.namespace`: `shared`, `platform`, or `deployment` depending on component (see Namespace Layout)
- `syncPolicy.automated.selfHeal: true` and `prune: true`
- `syncPolicy.syncOptions: [CreateNamespace=true]`
- `source.repoURL`: use `http://forgejo-http.deployment.svc.cluster.local:3000/stackable/openmetadata-dbt-demo.git` for Forgejo sources

## Commands

- `just deploy` — bootstrap the cluster with stackablectl (installs ArgoCD, Forgejo, then ArgoCD takes over)
- `just seal-secrets` — re-seal all plaintext secrets from `secrets/` into `platform/manifests/`
</system-reminder>

# Handover: openmetadata-dbt-demo debugging (2026-10-05)

Context for a fresh session. The previous session only had the repo's `dags/` directory mounted
as `/workspace` (no `.git`), so it worked in a separate clone. Restart with the repo root mounted.

> This file lives in `dags/`, which is git-synced into Airflow. Move or delete it, don't commit it.

## Setup facts

- **Two remotes, always name which one when saying "push":**
  - **GitHub** `github.com/stackabletech/openmetadata-dbt-demo`: a fresh deploy (`just deploy`)
    makes the in-cluster Forgejo take a **one-time copy** of this repo
    (`infrastructure/forgejo-manifests/configure-forgejo.yaml`, `mirror = false`). New clusters
    only see what's on GitHub.
  - **Forgejo (in-cluster)** `stackable/openmetadata-dbt-demo`, service `forgejo-http.deployment:3000`:
    ArgoCD on a running cluster syncs from here. All apps have automated sync + prune + selfHeal,
    so pushing to Forgejo deploys right away.
  - Working branch: `feat/data2day`. GitHub and Forgejo were both at `b482bc3` when checked.
- Repo `CLAUDE.md` golden rule: no `kubectl apply`/`helm install`; everything goes through Git + ArgoCD.
- Cluster: AKS context `data5day` (also `data3day` in the kubeconfig). `dags/kubeconfig` holds
  admin credentials. **Confirm it's gitignored** (`git check-ignore -v dags/kubeconfig`).
- Forgejo access from the workstation: `kubectl -n deployment port-forward svc/forgejo-http 3300:3000`.

## The demo (dags/)

`tpch_dbt_dag.py`, DAG `dbt_tpch_demo` (`@once`, Astronomer Cosmos):
`wait_for_services` (sensor: OM reachable + Trino schema `hive-iceberg.demo`, reschedule mode,
40 min timeout) → `dbt_tpch` (Cosmos task group, one KubernetesExecutor pod per dbt model,
virtualenv mode, uploads `run_results.json` shards to Garage `s3://dbt-artifacts/_runs/...`) →
`finalize_dbt_artifacts` (merge shards, `dbt docs generate`, publish manifest/catalog/run_results
to `s3://dbt-artifacts/tpch_demo/`) → `trigger_om_metadata_ingestion` → `trigger_om_dbt_ingestion`
(Keycloak password-grant token as `demo-admin`).
`dbt/tpch_demo`: 8 staging views over `tpch.tiny` + 6 mart tables in `hive-iceberg.demo`.

## Findings

### 1. DAG stalled: task pods Pending (CPU requests exhausted)
- Executor task pods request 1 CPU / 3 Gi (+ 250m vector). AirflowCluster
  `kubernetesExecutors.config.resources` is unset, so the operator defaults apply.
- User nodes were at 87–99 % CPU **requests** (actual usage ~4 %). Biggest consumers: Trino
  workers 1250m each, OpenSearch 1250m, each Airflow component 850m, NiFi 750m, Kafka brokers 600m.
- `wait_for_services` pod Pending with `Insufficient cpu`. The sensor's 40 min timeout started at
  first poke, so the run on data5day had probably timed out / is retrying.
- Minor: `opa-server-default-wntdd` (DaemonSet pod on the small system node) Pending for CPU. Harmless.

**Done:** commit `afd2df1` "Free cluster CPU: stop NiFi, scale Kafka brokers and Trino workers to 1"
- `platform/manifests/nifi/nifi.yaml`: `clusterOperation.stopped: true`
- `platform/manifests/kafka/kafka.yaml`: brokers `replicas: 1` (controllers left at 3)
- `platform/manifests/trino/trino.yaml`: workers `replicas: 1`

**Still open (better fix):** set smaller executor pod resources in the AirflowCluster spec
(e.g. 250m CPU / 1 Gi). Each dbt model still needs its own task pod.

### 2. OpenMetadata SSO: "Implicit flow is disabled for the client"
- OM runs with chart defaults `AUTHENTICATION_CLIENT_TYPE=public`, `AUTHENTICATION_RESPONSE_TYPE=id_token`
  (implicit flow). The Keycloak client `openmetadata` (`infrastructure/keycloak-manifests/configure-keycloak.yaml`)
  is CONFIDENTIAL, standard flow only, so Keycloak rejects the login.
- Considered: switching OM to a confidential client / code flow (`AUTHENTICATION_CLIENT_TYPE=confidential`
  + `OIDC_*` envs + OM's `/api/v1/system/config/jwks` in public keys). Written, then **dropped**.
- **Decision:** enable implicit flow in Keycloak, because a fresh deploy on a new cluster is planned.
  On an existing cluster this wouldn't apply: `configure-keycloak` is a one-off Job running OpenTofu
  with local state, and ArgoCD only replaces it when the Job spec changes.
- **Change (uncommitted in the clone):** `implicit_flow_enabled = true` on the `openmetadata`
  `keycloak_openid_client`, with a comment.
- **Known trade-off:** `valid_redirect_uris = ["*"]` + implicit flow lets anyone with a crafted login
  link receive tokens at an arbitrary redirect. Consider restricting to `http://<node-ip>:30585/callback`
  (node IP is only known at deploy time). Implicit flow is also deprecated (RFC 9700, removed in OAuth 2.1).

## State of the changes

All in the throwaway clone at `dags/openmetadata-dbt-demo/` (remotes `github`, `forgejo`):
- committed, unsigned: `afd2df1` (finding 1)
- uncommitted: Keycloak implicit flow (finding 2)

The user's own checkout showed `feat/data2day` diverged from `origin/feat/data2day` (1 commit each side)
for unrelated reasons. Not yet investigated: check `git remote -v` and
`git log --oneline --left-right origin/feat/data2day...HEAD`.

## Next steps

1. Sort out the divergence in the real checkout.
2. Bring the changes over, then delete the clone:
   ```
   git fetch dags/openmetadata-dbt-demo feat/data2day
   git cherry-pick afd2df1

   rm -rf dags/openmetadata-dbt-demo
